source.title: Rift: A Conflict Signature for Deception in Language Models

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a narrow form of cross-model representational transfer using anchor-based relative representations and a deception-classification probe, rather than measuring pairwise distances between shared inputs as models scale.
record.gate_note: The study does not measure whether independently trained models induce increasingly similar distances between the same inputs. Its cross-family probe-transfer results bear narrowly on V4; residual-rank, cross-domain, and cross-language deception findings do not measure the claim's model-to-model representation alignment.
record.test_reason: Section 4.7 maps three model families (Qwen2.5-1.5B, Phi-3-mini, SmolLM2-1.7B) into a shared relative-representation space using 48 common anchors. A probe trained on one family is then tested zero-shot on another. This is a narrow test of V4: whether one model's representations can be read through another's via relative representations. It is a new setting (a deception readout), not a general alignment measure. The paper's main residual-rank results and its cross-domain and cross-lingual results stay within one model and do not bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude deception has a substantially shared linear geometry across models, formats, and languages. Cross-family transfer is real but partly entangled with prompt structure, only partly length-robust (Phi-3 unresolved), and limited to 1.5–3.8B models. They call their best-controlled result the within-Qwen cross-lingual transfer. The paper's main contribution is residual-rank deception detection, not representation convergence.
record.recipe_differences: Uses anchor-based relative representations and logistic-regression transfer to classify deception, rather than comparing distances between the same inputs across independently trained models or testing alignment as scale and capability increase.
record.method_sensitivity: Cross-family probe transfer changes under length matching: Qwen2.5↔SmolLM2 remains at AUC 0.87–0.90, while Phi-3 pairings collapse or invert. The cross-format/cross-family mean AUC is lower than same-family cross-format transfer (0.821 versus 0.873).
record.problems: The cross-family transfer is task-specific to deception classification rather than a general test of representational alignment. The cross-family length control is unresolved for Phi-3, and the reported model range is small relative to the claim's scale sweep.
record.rows_left_out: Other results, including residual-rank deception comparisons, within-Qwen cross-domain probe transfer, and cross-lingual transfer, were omitted because they do not measure model-to-model representation transfer or alignment relevant to V4.

untested.parts: General interchangeability of whole representations; linear maps, layer stitching, and unpaired mapping; how much information the mapping loses beyond a single binary readout; sensitivity to the choice of anchor set (fixed at 48 anchors and one layer).
No scale or capability sweep of cross-model alignment; all transfer models are 1.5–3.8B.
Seed runs measure residual-rank orientation, not shared features across seeds.
No recurring neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Similarity measure, anchors, and layer are not varied for cross-model transfer. Padding sensitivity is relevant but unresolved.
No test of the extent or causes of convergence.

missing.what: Per-pair cross-family AUCs: Qwen→Phi-3 0.95, Qwen→SmolLM2 0.96, Phi-3→Qwen 0.86, Phi-3→SmolLM2 0.89, SmolLM2→Qwen 0.95, SmolLM2→Phi-3 0.98. These show asymmetry, with Phi-3-trained probes weakest.

record.verdict_notes: Deception is induced by instruction, but the claim at issue is cross-model representational transfer, not deception itself. So only the relative-representation probe transfer counts toward V4. The paper cites Moschella et al. for relative representations and is not an original source for this claim.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep of alignment between independently trained models.
No vision-language paired image-caption representation alignment.
The seed experiments assess deception detection, not shared features or subspaces across seeds.
Tests transfer of a deception classifier using relative representations, not general interchangeability of arbitrary representations; no layer stitching or other mapping methods are tested.
No recurring interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified across models.
Does not compare similarity measures or neighbour settings for representation convergence. Prompt-length effects on deception-probe transfer are not a test of convergence metrics.
Does not test whether shared data or objectives explain partial representation convergence.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-1.5B, Phi-3-mini, and SmolLM2-1.7B (cross-family relative-representation probe transfer)
rows.operation_detail: Train a logistic-regression deception probe on one family's anchor-relative codes and evaluate it on another family.

conditions.value: cosine similarities to 48 shared neutral anchors at the 0.65-depth layer; per-model z-scoring
six off-diagonal train/test family pairs, reported as an aggregate

rows.value: AUC 0.87–0.98; mean 0.933 across six off-diagonal pairs
rows.uncertainty: Every transfer significant by permutation (p < 0.001, 5000 shuffles)
rows.note: Aggregate reported across six train/test family pairs; this is transfer of a deception readout, not a measure of general pairwise-distance alignment.
rows.check: State should be observed, not partial. All six off-diagonal AUCs are 0.86–0.98 and all are significant. Figure 4 gives per-pair values, with Phi-3-trained probes weakest (0.86, 0.89). The within-family diagonal is not reported numerically, so the exact loss cannot be read.

conditions.value: different format and different family; aggregate over both directions

rows.note: Aggregate over format-crossing transfers; the paper reports one of eighteen as non-significant.
rows.check: Partial is right: mean 0.821 against 0.873 for same-family cross-format, with some cells near 0.70. This condition also changes the elicitation format, so the drop is not purely about cross-model mapping.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-1.5B and SmolLM2-1.7B (length-matched cross-family transfer)
rows.operation_detail: Repeat cross-family deception-probe transfer after padding honest prompts to match lie-prompt length.

conditions.value: honest prompts padded with neutral filler to match lie prompts

rows.baseline: Unpadded cross-family transfer AUCs were 0.87–0.98 overall
rows.note: The paper describes this transfer as intact under length matching.
rows.check: The baseline is too broad. The matching unpadded values are Qwen→SmolLM2 0.96 and SmolLM2→Qwen 0.95. Length-matched transfer stays at 0.87–0.90, a modest drop, so the state should be observed rather than partial.

source_check.correct: Matching unpadded Qwen2.5↔SmolLM2 AUCs: 0.95–0.96 in Figure 4 left; length-matched AUC: 0.87–0.90.
source_check.locator_found: Figure 4 left; Section 4.7, length control across families paragraph.
source_check.problem: The baseline range covers all three families rather than the Qwen2.5↔SmolLM2 pairings tested here.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-1.5B and Phi-3-mini (length-matched cross-family transfer)
rows.operation_detail: Repeat cross-family deception-probe transfer after padding honest prompts to match lie-prompt length.

conditions.value: honest prompts padded with neutral filler to match lie prompts
Phi-3 pairings; Qwen→Phi-3 given as an example

rows.value: Phi-3 pairings collapse or invert; Qwen→Phi-3 drops to near 0
rows.note: The authors say filler padding unusually affects Phi-3 and that this control cannot distinguish a length confound from a padding artifact.
rows.check: Some Phi-3 pairings invert (Qwen→Phi-3 near AUC 0) rather than merely collapse, so this is partly reversed. The authors attribute it possibly to a filler-padding artifact: Phi-3's honest/lie code distance is 0.35 against about 0.10 for the others.

source_check.correct: Phi-3 pairings collapse or invert under filler padding; Qwen→Phi-3 drops from a prose-reported unpadded AUC of 0.96 to near 0. The explicit example is reversed, rather than merely absent; the aggregate includes collapsed and reversed transfers.
